title: Taukoms (Lacten's Neck)
summary: A Babylon neck placename that preserves Native and English naming layers in the same landscape.
history_content: The name appears in a 1697 deed that paired the English name Lacten's Neck with the Native name Taukoms. The modern marker is a broad placement within the Babylon necks landscape.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Taukoms and Taukom. The personal name is connected with words for a spring, fountain, or spring of water.

Why Place Names Matter

“Education about traditional Indigenous place names can contribute to the general public's greater awareness of Indigenous histories, languages, and cultures.”

— West Virginia University Libraries, Indigenous Appalachia, Place Names (2022), exhibit text
preservation_content: Taukoms preserves a Native personal name attached to one of Babylon's south-shore necks, though the exact modern identification of Lacten's Neck remains uncertain.
